title: Inspection video no longer replays the same stretch
description:
After the streaming ladder went in, an inspection video would play about fifteen seconds, play that same stretch again, and only then move on. It could do that more than once in a file, at normal speed and at 5×.

The pictures in the stream were not duplicated. The player was forcing a quality change by throwing away the buffer it had already loaded. The browser jumped back to the start of that buffer, so the same stretch played again. It did this twice in a row: once to drop to a lighter step, and once when it turned automatic selection back on. On videos that were still playing from the original file at high speed, the ahead-buffer also sent the same group of frames a second time, which looked like the same loop.

Quality changes now only affect the next piece that is fetched. Playback keeps moving forward from the current time. The lighter and middle steps are still keyed about every two seconds, including on slower camera frame rates, so a refill stays short. The original file is still copied, not re-encoded. The 5× cap is unchanged: on an 80 Mbps connection the player stays on a step that fits, and a 25 Mbps original at 5× still needs about 125 Mbps so that top step stays off. Video bytes still come straight from Wasabi. The same behavior is on pipeshare.live and pipeshare.net.

Who is affected: PipeShare playback in the browser. Hard-refresh the page. If a video is already open, close it and open it again.
changeLog: Playback no longer jumps back when the player changes quality. The same stretch is not played twice.
Fast playback of an original file that is not on the ladder yet no longer re-sends the same frames.
A ladder rebuild keeps the current timestamp instead of restarting the buffered window.
Encoded steps place a keyframe about every two seconds at the camera's real frame rate.
5× on a typical 80 Mbps connection still uses the middle step. The original is still copied and is used only when the link can feed it.
